ocr.notes: Gist right but errors: Wilson 'a fair man' (not 'big'); 'Elliott fizzle' (not 'El Rio'); 'came on a visit to see his friends' omitted; cup on 'Mr. Sheppard's sideboard of the Abbey', 'nearly twenty-four inches in height', inscribed 'champion boxer of England', dated May 22, 1878 (not 1875). An ink smear covers parts of a few lines about Wilson opening a public house and Sullivan.

summary.suggested: The Cleveland Leader, quoting the Boston Star, reported that Tom Allen had just arrived from England and was resting at Patsy Sheppard's in Boston, planning a few weeks in New York and possibly exhibitions.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Cleveland Leader, Wednesday Morning, November 1, 1882. article.json has no focus field.

facts.fact: Allen arrived in Boston from England and stayed at Patsy Sheppard's sporting resort on Hayward Place
Allen planned to go from Boston to New York for a few weeks, likely giving exhibitions, before returning to England, saying he had not come to fight anyone but to visit friends
Allen called Tug Wilson a 'faker' for skipping out on his backer Richard K. Fox, and judged John L. Sullivan, whom he had never met, the best man in the world
Allen had a silver cup presented to him as 'champion boxer of England' by his backers and admirers on May 22, 1878, at Cambridge Hall, Newman Street, Oxford Street, London
places: Cambridge Hall, Newman Street, Oxford Street, London

notes: Allen's opinions are reported in indirect speech, so no verbatim quote. Article gives his age as forty-three.
